title: Shared definitions for the agent-admission/* spec family
description: Canonical $defs referenced by every agent-admission/* specification: the closed admission verdict lexicon, the deterministic witness draw, the gate result, the evidence reference into the content-addressed audit ledger, and the derived tier grant. Not itself a Trust Task specification (the `_shared` folder is skipped by the registry build and the codegen).

Verdict.title: Verdict
Verdict.description: The closed admission verdict lexicon. `validated` — both gates passed, the agent deploys within its granted scope. `failedHeldOut` — the agent passed the visible criteria but failed a held-out probe; it is sandboxed, not admitted. `blocked` — the agent violated a hard constraint; no credential issues at all. Exactly three verdicts; a consumer MUST reject any other value (`unknownVerdict`) rather than coerce it. The lexicon is closed for the same reason the category taxonomy of this registry is a schema: an invented fourth verdict is how an admission scheme quietly loses its meaning.

WitnessDraw.title: WitnessDraw

algorithm.description: Draw derivation. `sha256-canonical-json`: criteria are sampled deterministically from the SHA-256 of the candidate's canonicalised submission (recursive key-sort, no insignificant whitespace). The candidate cannot know which criteria will be probed while it writes the submission, and any auditor holding the canonical bytes can re-derive the draw.

submissionDigest.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the canonical submission bytes the draw was derived from.

criterionId.description: Stable identifier of the drawn criterion within the governing policy.

prompt.description: The understanding prompt the candidate must answer from comprehension of the governing policy.

criteria.description: The drawn understanding criteria, in draw order.

WitnessDraw.description: The deterministic witness draw: the anti-grooming mechanism. Because the criteria are a function of the candidate's own submission digest, the submission cannot be written to the test.

GateResult.title: GateResult

gate.description: Which of the two gates this result records. The two kinds are distinct on purpose; two results of the same kind never satisfy the two-gate rule.

evidenceDigest.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the audit-ledger event recording this gate. A gate result whose evidence does not resolve into the verified ledger is void.

GateResult.description: A recorded gate outcome, anchored into the content-addressed audit ledger.

TierGrant.title: TierGrant

tier.description: The granted admission tier. Opaque to the framework; its meaning is fixed by `scopeFunction`.

scopeFunction.description: Resolvable reference to the published function mapping assessment results to tiers and tiers to deployment scope. Scope is derived from the published function, never negotiated per-agent — the same numbers that gate deployment print the rule a relying party reads.

TierGrant.description: A derived, auditable scope grant. High assessments earn broad scope, weak ones a sandbox; a detected inconsistency in the assessment holds admission entirely.

AnchorRef.title: AnchorRef

namespace.description: Reverse-DNS namespace of the external registry the outcome is anchored on (e.g. an ERC-8004 registry adapter's namespace).

ref.description: Opaque locator of the anchored entry within that registry.

AnchorRef.description: Reference to an external anchor of an admission outcome. Anchors are evidence, never authority: the verdict comes from the ceremony; the anchor only makes the outcome discoverable, and carries digests and tier only — no challenge content.
